name: The 1v1 Lobby Says When It Cannot Connect (blocked sign-in, 13 languages)
note: Written with the gate on 2026-09-29, from the red team that found the Japanese overflow (SudokuDiary 56). The gate serves dist, so every mutation rebuilds.

mutations.name: the search stops asking whether it can reach the server
mutations.why: With sign-in failing, the player watches the radar for twelve seconds and is then told nobody was found — the BT-2 behaviour this gate exists to keep out.

mutations.name: a failed sign-in is not tried again
mutations.why: One dropped network at the first search locks 1v1 out until the app restarts; lifting the block changes nothing.

mutations.name: the failure text goes back to break-word
mutations.why: Japanese has no spaces; with keep-all the whole sentence is one unbreakable run and pushes 21px out of the pill on a 360px phone.

mutations.name: the no-opponent card loses Search again
mutations.why: Added 2026-10-07 (BACKLOG D10). Without it a player who wanted a person can only take the AI or close the lobby and start over.

mutations.name: Search again opens the AI lobby instead of searching
mutations.why: A button that says search and does something else; the step presses it and waits for the radar.
mutations.find: <button type="button" className="btn btn-primary w-100 btn-search-again" onClick={handleQuickMatch}>
mutations.replace: <button type="button" className="btn btn-primary w-100 btn-search-again" onClick={handlePlayAi}>
mutations.expectFailure: did not start a new search

mutations.name: the could-not-connect card offers Search again too
mutations.why: Searching again from a phone that cannot reach the server repeats the same failure; the card points to the AI match instead.
